chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about passionate love (al-'ishq), so he said:
Hearts that became empty of the remembrance of God, so God made them taste the love of other than Him.

key_terms.العشق: Al-'Ishq: Passionate, obsessive love — often used to describe overwhelming worldly attachment
key_terms.ذكر الله: Dhikr Allah: Remembrance of God — the spiritual practice of keeping God in one's consciousness

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the nature of passionate love (al-'ishq) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked about the nature of passionate love (al-'ishq) by his companion al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. The Imam explained that al-'ishq is a spiritual affliction resulting from hearts becoming devoid of God's remembrance. In this teaching, addressed to the scholarly circle in 8th-century Kufa, the Imam presents worldly obsessive attachment as a consequence of spiritual emptiness, implying that true fulfillment comes only through devotion to God.
